chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in a man entering into ihram wearing a known (distinctive) garment, and leaving it is more preferable to me if he is able to wear another. And it is disliked to sell a garment in which the muhrim has entered into ihram.' He narrated that.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.اَلثَّوْبِ اَلْمُعْلَمِ: A known or distinctive garment (as opposed to generic cloth)
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: To enter into the state of Ihram
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (a legal ruling indicating preference against an action)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear a specific or distinctive garment while in the state of Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while wearing a marked or specific garment is legally valid for ihram, preferring an unmarked one reflects the ideal of simplicity and detachment from worldly distinctions. This ruling is further contextualized by the prohibition of selling the garment worn during ihram, emphasizing the sanctity of the state of consecration. The preference for generic clothing aligns with the Shia emphasis on humility and equality among pilgrims, mirroring the Prophet's practice.
